summary: Iteration 31 (WEB, frontend-only): validated NO regression from the new /app/frontend/src/lib/videoCompress.js import chain. Four flows executed against the live preview with founder credentials, all passing with ZERO JS errors and ZERO 'Upload failed'/'Upload network error' toasts: (1) Home composer small-video upload (151KB /tmp/small.mp4) — composer-progress appeared with phase 'Uploading' (saw_uploading=True, saw_compressing=False, confirming files under TARGET_MAX_BYTES=95MB SKIP the compressor as designed), composer-preview-video rendered, Post button produced 'Posted!' toast; (2) Home composer photo upload (7.5KB /tmp/sample.jpg) — composer-preview-image rendered, no Compressing phase ever appears for images, 'Posted!' toast fired (images correctly bypass the video compressor branch); (3) /videos/new small-video upload (151KB /tmp/small.mp4) — single-shot Cloudinary path unchanged, video-url-input populated with https://res.cloudinary.com/dpnrol54k/video/upload/…/small_ft0lfg.mp4, Publish button navigated to /profile with 'Video uploaded' + 'Video published to your profile!' toasts visible; (4) videoCompress.js import chain does NOT break either page — PostComposer.jsx and VideoUpload.jsx both mount and are fully interactive, 0 console errors and 0 pageerrors captured across the entire run. The >95MB compression trigger cannot be exercised headlessly with a small sample (as noted in the review request) — verified instead that the branch is dead-code-safe for sub-threshold files and that canCompressVideo()/compressVideoToTarget imports evaluate without side effects at module load.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/lib/videoCompress.js:105 and /app/frontend/src/pages/VideoUpload.jsx:53-55 use inconsistent progress conventions. compressVideoToTarget calls onProgress with a FRACTION [0..1] (Math.min(0.99, currentTime/duration)). PostComposer.jsx (line 42) correctly converts via Math.round(f*100). VideoUpload.jsx (line 54) passes onProgress: setProgress directly, so `progress` state gets 0..1 during compression, and the render at line 146 does `Math.round(progress * 100)` — that's fine for the compression phase. BUT the same `progress` state is later reused by uploadToCloudinary onProgress at line 63 (also 0..1 in cloudinary.js), which is then displayed as Math.round(progress*100) — this is self-consistent. However PostComposer stores `progress` as 0..100 integers (line 51 `Math.round(f * 100)`) and displays `{progress}%`. Mixed conventions across the two callers make the code brittle; recommend picking one (either fractions everywhere or percents everywhere).

/app/frontend/src/lib/videoCompress.js:109 `await srcVideo.play()` requires an autoplay-permissible context. Because the file was picked via a user gesture (file input change) autoplay generally succeeds, but Chrome will silently reject play() if the tab has been backgrounded. In that case srcVideo.onended never fires and the awaited Promise hangs forever with no timeout — the composer will look 'stuck at Compressing 0%' with no way out. Add a wall-clock watchdog (e.g., reject if currentTime hasn't advanced for 5s) and honor `signal.abort()` from a user-facing Cancel button (the AbortSignal wiring exists but no UI exposes it).

/app/frontend/src/lib/videoCompress.js:87 `srcCapture.getAudioTracks().forEach((t) => canvasStream.addTrack(t))` — if the source has NO audio tracks (some phone screen-recordings, silent .mov exports) MediaRecorder still starts fine, but if it has multiple audio tracks only the LAST one plays (canvas.captureStream() doesn't mix). For most videos this is fine, but worth documenting.

/app/frontend/src/lib/videoCompress.js:98 recorder.onstop set BEFORE recorder.start — good — but the awaited `stopped` Promise never rejects on `recorder.onerror`. A MediaRecorder codec fault (rare, but happens on some Firefox builds w/ vp9) will emit `error` then `stop`, and the returned Blob will be empty (chunks=[]). Callers would upload a 0-byte file to Cloudinary. Add: `recorder.onerror = (e) => reject(new Error(e.error?.message || 'Recorder error'))`.

/app/frontend/src/lib/videoCompress.js:136 `return out.size < file.size ? {file: out, wasCompressed: true} : {file, wasCompressed: false}` — if the re-encode failed to shrink (e.g. duration was miscalculated or MediaRecorder produced a bloated container) we return the ORIGINAL file, which is still >95MB, and the caller then hands it straight to uploadToCloudinary — which will fall into the chunked path (>90MB) and eventually succeed OR fail with the same 'Upload network error' the previous iteration was fixing. Consider a hard-fail toast in that case so the user knows compression didn't help.

/app/frontend/src/components/PostComposer.jsx:39 vs VideoUpload.jsx:51 — both call the same TARGET_MAX_BYTES threshold, but VideoUpload sets phase='compressing' (lowercase) while PostComposer sets phase='Compressing' (title case). Cosmetic, but caused a mismatch bug earlier in the codebase — pull the label into a constant or lowercase-and-capitalize at render time.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The >95MB compression happy-path was NOT exercised end-to-end (impossible headlessly without generating a 95MB+ real-time-encoded video, and the compressor itself takes ~duration-of-clip minutes to run because MediaRecorder is real-time). Both call sites of compressVideoToTarget correctly gate on file.size > TARGET_MAX_BYTES (95MB) so sub-threshold uploads bypass the compressor entirely — this was verified via the composer-progress label which read 'Uploading' (not 'Compressing') during a 151KB video upload. If a future iteration wants to force-exercise the compression branch, the cleanest approach is to (a) monkey-patch TARGET_MAX_BYTES to something like 1MB in a dev build, or (b) drive it via a Playwright script that first uses browser FS APIs to create a >95MB Blob and hands it to the file input via DataTransfer — the encoder itself works (main agent already verified canvas.captureStream + MediaRecorder in-browser). Selectors used this run and still stable: [data-testid=post-composer], composer-caption, composer-add-photo, composer-add-video (backed by hidden inputs with accept=image/* and accept=video/*), composer-preview-image, composer-preview-video, composer-progress (only present while uploading, text = '<phase> <int>%'), composer-submit; on /videos/new: video-upload-form, #video-upload (hidden input), video-url-input, video-title-input, video-publish-btn.
rca of the issue: No bug reproduced. All regression checks passed. The videoCompress.js addition is import-safe (no top-level side effects; canCompressVideo() is only called lazily inside compressVideoToTarget when triggered) and the two call sites correctly short-circuit for files under 95MB, so no code path that previously worked has changed for typical uploads.
